text:
anya: Quick sync — after the driver bump last week we saw cache hit-rate drop and p99 token latency +12% on 6B/13B runs. I think churn + mismatched kernel paths is the root. proposing an "adaptive cache cohorting" approach. TL;DR: cohort cache keys by (model_variant, driver_epoch, seqlen_bin), persist cohorts to local SSD with epoch headers, and use driver/runtime signals to do fast invalidation. Thoughts?

mike: can you paste the perf numbers we saw?

anya: sure — from profiling (last 48h):
- baseline (pre-bump) p50/p95/p99 token latency: 18/42/96 ms
- post-bump: 19/47/108 ms
- KV cache hit-rate dropped from 84% -> 63% for common prefixes
- CPU cost up ~7% from extra kernel selection branching and cache misses

priya: ugh. that hit-rate drop is big. do we know keys that changed?

anya: some keys were identical, but driver_epoch in key header changed due to new runtime ABI heuristics; workers started routing to seqlen-dependent kernels and KV layout changed semantics for cached KV blobs. so old entries became incompatible at runtime.

sam: idea: rather than globally nuking cache on driver change, we keep old cohorts around for a grace period and route requests to cohort-compatible GPUs until cleanup. less tail pain.

eva: +1. we should avoid synchronous deletes; async scrub + cohorted TTL. also need to ensure disk persistence format is explicit about the runtime ABI.

anya: exactly. proposed key format (simple):
```
key := "model:" + model_id + ":variant:" + variant + ":drev:" + driver_epoch + ":sbin:" + seqlen_bin + ":h:" + sha256(prefix)
```
- driver_epoch: monotonic integer bumped on driver/runtime build or kernel selector change
- seqlen_bin: coarse bucket e.g., 1-32,33-128,129-512,>512
- prefix hash: first N tokens hashed to avoid huge keys

priya: how do we compute driver_epoch reliably across dedicated/private deployments?

anya: driver_epoch comes from the control plane: the driver-agent reports a "driver_build_id" + selector_config_hash on startup. control plane assigns a compact epoch (int) per unique tuple and distributes it. agents write the epoch into cohort headers.

mike: if we persist cohorts on SSD, how do we handle space + eviction?

anya: cohorts are first-class namespaces. eviction policy: LRU within cohort, and cohorts themselves have retention windows. heuristics: high-volume cohorts (popular variant+seqlen) get larger quota; stale cohorts (old driver_epoch) get low quota and asynchronous reclamation.

sam: what about model rollouts / canary -> variant changes?

anya: model variant changes increment variant tag in key (we already have variant). when a canary is promoted, we give the new cohort an initial cold-warm phase: keep old cohort for 24-72h to reduce warm-start regressions. also record per-prompt hit_rate_by_cohort metric.

eva: we need observability hooks: gauge cohort_hit_rate, cohort_eviction_rate, avg_kv_blob_size, seqbin_hit_rate. also correlate with kernel-path selection logs.

priya: any risk that driver_epoch churn will explode number of cohorts? e.g., frequent infra rollouts?

anya: to limit cardinality we canonicalize epoch at region/cluster level and only bump on meaningful selector/runtime ABI changes. tiny infra patches don't force epoch bump. if we do an emergency rollback, the control plane can emit a "compatibility_view" mapping to treat some epochs as compatible for read-paths.

mike: can we make read-path tolerant? read-verify: attempt to read cached blob, validate header+kernelsig, and if mismatch, treat as miss but enqueue async re-encode of prefix into current cohort. that reduces cold miss p99s.

anya: yep — read-verify + async repair is key. flow:
1) lookup cohort key (current epoch) -> if hit, verify kernel_sig in header matches local runtime; if mismatch, treat as miss and return;
2) if miss, serve from model, but enqueue a background task to repopulate cohort for faster warm-up;
3) background task may check older compatible cohorts to copy blobs (fast copy on same host) if allowed.

sam: what's the enforcement surface for "kernel_sig"? where do we compute signature?

anya: kernel_sig computed from (kernel_selector_version, seqlen_bin, quantization_profile_id). combined into a short hash stored in the blob header.

priya: need to ensure security: cached blobs might be shared between tenants on Dedicated — must namespace with customer id and acl.

anya: yes, cohort namespace includes tenant_id for dedicated/private. hosted uses tenant isolation at process level; still include tenant_id in key.

eva: regression mitigation plan? rollback path?

anya: plan: staged rollouts:
- canary -> monitor cohort_hit_rate, p99 token latency, kernel-selection-mismatch metric
- if mismatch rate > 5% or p99 > threshold, control plane doesn't bump global epoch; instead emits compatibility mapping and schedules opt-in slow migration.

mike: implementation risks: more complexity around on-disk structures + GC. dev effort estimate?

anya: rough: 3 eng-sprints for runtime + agent + control plane bits, plus 1 sprint for metrics/console. sam/priya — assume resources?

sam: ok but split: core runtime (cohort namespace + read-verify + async repair) 2 sprints; control plane epoch management 1 sprint; SSD persistence + GC 1 sprint. observability + rollout logic 1 sprint. total 5 if parallel.

priya: +1 from security POV; need design doc for ACL + encryption-at-rest for persisted cohorts.

deploy-bot: [deploy] cohorting-proposal doc posted: https://redwood.docs/internal/eng-runtime/cohorting-proposal-1899 (draft) :rocket:

anya: I'll write the doc and include microbenchmarks. quick perf expectation: if hit-rate recovers to 80% we should see p99 drop back ~10-12ms and CPU overhead removed. also reduces cross-GPU copy by keeping compatible blobs local.

mike: sounds reasonable. next: can you add a short prototype that shows read-verify + async repair? even something in Python with on-disk mocks.

anya: will do. I'll open a PR with prototype + draft doc today. thanks all :raised_hands:
